jobs.description: LiveRamp is shaping the future of responsible data collaboration between the world’s leading brands, retailers, financial services providers, and healthcare innovators. As consumers embrace new AI-driven experiences, the LiveRamp data collaboration network exponentially expands the breadth and accuracy of the data on which marketing AI capabilities operate, powering deeper customer insight and measurable performance on a global scale. LiveRamp is headquartered in San Francisco, California, with offices worldwide. Learn more at LiveRamp.com . We are looking for a highly-motivated, business-minded Legal and Data Ethics Operations Analyst. This person will help the Data Ethics and Legal teams solve internal problems, implement goal-oriented strategies and play a key role in the Data Ethics team. This role strengthens operational execution across jurisdictions through process improvement, responsible AI enablement, privacy and legal operations, playbook development, and effective management of data subject requests. You will: Coordinate data subject request management, including intake, categorization, routing, deadline tracking, documentation, communications, and closure; work with the Data Ethics team on high-risk, complex, sensitive, or multi-jurisdictional requests. Build and maintain practical playbooks, decision trees, checklists, templates, escalation criteria, and role-based guidance for recurring data ethics, privacy, legal, and regulatory processes. Manage privacy questionnaire workflows by coordinating intake, preparing AI-assisted first drafts from approved information, maintaining supporting evidence, and escalating questions requiring legal, privacy, security, or data ethics judgment. Support the design of responsible AI controls including approved-source use, permissions, confidentiality, traceability, version control, audit trails, quality checks, and human approval before material outputs are used. jobs.title: Director Commercial Legal, EMEA
jobs.description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role   We are seeking a UK-based Director, Commercial Legal to lead Veeam’s EMEA Commercial Legal team, supporting our fast-paced sales organization. Reporting to the Senior Director, Commercial Legal, based in the UK, you will lead a team of four to five lawyers while remaining a key individual contributor.   This highly visible, hands-on leadership role combines team oversight with direct involvement in complex software transactions. You will serve as the team’s escalation point while negotiating and closing strategic deals. The ideal candidate is an experienced technology commercial lawyer and proven people leader who thrives in a collaborative environment and stays closely connected to the business .   What You’ll Do   Partner closely with your US counterpart to drive consistency across contracting positions, templates, playbooks, and processes, while sharing knowledge, best practices, and workload across regions.    Negotiate and close a significant portfolio of complex, high-value agreements, including software, SaaS, BaaS, professional services, and channel transactions, partnering directly with Sales, Deal Desk, and other key stakeholders.    Provide clear, practical, and commercially focused legal advice, balancing legal, regulatory, privacy, and commercial consideration

jobs.title: Webdesigner (w/m/d)
jobs.description: Einleitung Wir sind auf der Suche nach neuen Kollegen! Migrando ist ein Legal-Tech-Unternehmen aus Cottbus. Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, den komplizierten und langwierigen Prozess der Einbürgerung effizienter und kundenfreundlicher zu gestalten. Mit unserer Expertise im Ausländerrecht, unserer juristischen Kompetenz und einem starken Team von zahlreichen Mitarbeitern begleiten wir tausende Mandanten erfolgreich auf dem Weg zur deutschen Staatsbürgerschaft. Am besten verschaffst du dir gleich einen Einblick unter migrando(.)de/karriere, unserer Karriere-Page. Denn wir können hier schreiben was wir wollen, im Endeffekt bleibt es eine langweilige Einleitung. Uns ist egal, welche Zertifikate du hast oder wo du studiert hast. Was uns interessiert: Was kannst du wirklich? Wer jahrelang in der Praxis gearbeitet und Hands-on-Erfahrungen gesammelt hat, bringt mehr mit als jeder Kursabschluss. Wir suchen nach Kollegen, die im besten Fall mehrjährige Erfahrung mitbringen und bereit sind, Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Wir bieten Dir Bei uns erwartet dich ein Mix aus gestalterischer Freiheit und echtem Impact. Du arbeitest nicht an abstrakten Konzepten, die irgendwann vielleicht live gehen – sondern an Produkten, die täglich tausende Menschen sehen und nutzen. Dein Output ist sichtbar, messbar und macht einen Unterschied. Abwechslungsreiche Kreativprojekte Bei uns gestaltest du echte Produkte: von Landingpages für Rechtsberatung über Infoportale bis zu interaktiven Online-Assistenten. Zugang zu Premium-Tools Du arbeitest mit modernen Plugins und Tools wie Figma, Lovable, Bricks und Hubspot. Firmen-Zugänge für Adobe und Co. Selbstverständlich erhältst du bei dieser Stelle Zugriff auf die Adobe Creative Cloud und alle anderen Tools, die du brauchst. KI-Design Du darfst direkt Hand anlegen, wenn es darum geht, neue KI-Tools für deine Designs auszuprobieren. Vielleicht ergibt sich ein neuer Workflow für dich? Wir ermutigen unsere Mitarbeiter in vielen Bereichen, KI zu nutzen

jobs.title: Director, EMEA Government Affairs & Public Policy
jobs.description: Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake. Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital. The role in a nutshell: Our customers include some of the most regulated organizations in the world, and we have a strong and growing UK and European customer base. Europe is one of our highest-growth priorities. It is also where the rules for our category are actively being written — the Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, the EU AI Act, and the standards work running underneath all of them. We are hiring our first dedicated European government affairs and public policy leader to own that ground. You will set Chainguard’s European policy strategy, establish us as a trusted technical voice with the officials and bodies shaping cyber regulation on the continent and in the UK, and translate fast-moving policy into what it means for our positioning, our product, and our customers. What you'll do Set and own Chainguard’s European policy strategy — priorities, positions, target institutions and officials, and the narrative we take into the policy process. Engage governments, regulators, and standards bodies across Europe and the UK, including the European Commission (notably DG CNECT and DG GROW), the European Parliament, ENISA, and the standards bodies — CEN-CENELEC and ETSI — doing the technical work underneath the CRA and NIS2. jobs.description: Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without any hidden fees or compounding interest. Affirm’s International Compliance team designs and implements compliance programs that proactively address regulatory requirements while identifying and mitigating compliance risks. As a second line of defence function, Compliance partners closely with the business to support new products, markets, and strategic initiatives while strengthening controls and delivering strong consumer outcomes. As Regulatory Compliance Manager, Australia, you will lead the Australian regulatory compliance program. You will translate global compliance strategy into local execution, ensure applicable Australian regulatory and licensing obligations are met, and support responsible growth and strong consumer outcomes. What You’ll Do Australian Regulatory Program Ownership Own and oversee the Australian regulatory compliance framework for consumer credit and related financial services, including the National Consumer Credit Protection Act, National Credit Code, Privacy Act,, applicable licence conditions, and associated regulatory guidance. Maintain documented compliance arrangements that support Australian credit licence obligations and keep pace with regulatory change, including the rules applying to buy now pay later (low cost credit contracts) and consumer credit. Lead ASIC examinations, inquiries, information requests, licence interactions, and other supervisory engagement. Oversee timely and accurate regulatory notifications and reporting, including reportable situations, internal dispute resolution data, licence updates, and other applicable filings. jobs.title: Data Privacy Compliance Specialist
jobs.description: The Data Privacy Compliance Specialist supports DeepHealth's global data privacy programs, including HIPAA and GDPR. Reporting to the Data Privacy Compliance Lead, this role collaborates across the organization to help ensure personal data is collected, processed, and stored in line with applicable privacy laws and DeepHealth requirements. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Support organizational data privacy efforts and help ensure compliance with applicable local, national, and global privacy laws and regulations. Assist with the Privacy by Design program supporting product development and modification, including software and AI use cases. Collaborate with Vendor Management on vendor qualification and on implementation of Data Processing Agreements and Transfer Impact Assessments as applicable. Research and review country-specific data privacy frameworks and regulations to support continued compliance and business opportunities. Collaborate cross-functionally to implement technical and organizational measures that support data privacy. Monitor how personal data is collected, processed, and stored for compliance with applicable laws. Participate in investigations and impact assessments related to information security events with privacy implications. Serve as a backup point of contact for data protection authorities and data subjects, handling inquiries and requests. Collaborate cross-functionally to improve data privacy processes in support of risk management frameworks such as GDPR and HIPAA. Maintain clear documentation of privacy activities and support audit and regulatory readiness as assigned. Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience (required). Minimum of 2 years of experience in a regulated industry (required); medical device experience preferred. Software and/or Software as a Medical Device experience preferred.
